rules.verified: Independently checked before being shown as a verified mark. A recognised fishing publication can be the verification source for a published mark.
rules.community_unverified: Submitted by an angler but not independently checked.

marks.name: Benllech Bay
marks.description: Published SeaAngler fishing mark at Benllech Bay. The publication describes fishing close in and advises care around the higher ledges.
tips: SeaAngler reports that many fish can be taken close in.
SeaAngler advises particular care from the higher ledges.
marks.access: Visit Anglesey reports disabled facilities and access for disabled visitors. Fishing Wales reports fishing from the sand and promenade.

source.reference: Benllech Bay Sea Fishing Mark, published 17 June 2021
source.location_reference: British Beaches, Benllech Beach, approximate beach midpoint

marks.parking: Visit Anglesey confirms parking at Benllech Beach; parking charges may apply.

marks.name: Cemlyn Beach
marks.description: SeaAngler published Cemlyn Beach as an easily accessible Anglesey mark, reporting codling, whiting and pouting and noting that the rocks at the end of the beach can also be worth trying.
tips: SeaAngler reported fish between approximately 30 and 100 yards out.
SeaAngler reported that evening was the better time in that report.
The rocks at the end of the beach were reported as worth trying during the day.
marks.access: National Trust and AccessAble report a step-free entrance from the far end of the car park, but the wider coastal route includes gravel, shingle, uneven ground and gates. The shingle ridge is not suitable for wheelchairs.

source.reference: UK Sea Fishing Catch Reports 5.1.10, Anglesey section
source.location_reference: British Beaches, Cemlyn Beach, approximate beach midpoint
source.access_reference: Visit Anglesey, Countryside and coast at Cemlyn

marks.parking: Bryn Aber car park at Cemlyn. National Trust says the car park is affected by tides and should be checked against tide times.

marks.name: Garth Pier
marks.description: SeaAngler published Garth Pier as a sea-fishing venue, reporting bass to double figures along with cod, pollack, wrasse, mackerel and dogfish. The pier's current official visitor information confirms that fishing is currently permitted with a fishing pass.
marks.access: Fishing is permitted with a fishing pass. Current official information lists £3 for a day fishing pass and £10 annually.

source.reference: Book This Pier for Just a Quid, published 9 September 2009
source.location_reference: Garth Pier coordinates independently checked against published geographic sources

marks.parking: Garth Pier has on-site car parking. The official pier information lists £2 car parking and free parking for Blue Badge holders.

marks.name: Calshot
marks.description: SeaAngler published Calshot as a shallow sea-fishing venue at the mouth of Southampton Water.
tips: SeaAngler reports the venue generally fishes during the last three hours of the flood and first couple of hours of the ebb.
marks.access: The venue includes shingle beaches. Hampshire County Council confirms accessible parking and wheelchair access at the Activities Centre, but this does not establish wheelchair access to the fishing position.

source.reference: Calshot Sea Fishing Mark, published 18 May 2021
source.location_reference: British Beaches, Calshot Beach, approximate beach midpoint
source.current_location_reference: Hampshire County Council Calshot visitor information

marks.parking: Hampshire County Council confirms parking at Calshot Activities Centre; current local parking arrangements should be checked before travel.

marks.name: Sandwich Bay
marks.description: SeaAngler published Sandwich Bay as a sea-fishing mark and identifies the 10th green near the slipway as a popular mark.
tips: SeaAngler reports fishing from low water up to high water can produce catches.
SeaAngler reports coloured water, especially after a south-westerly blow, can be productive.
marks.access: The beachfront includes sandy, unsurfaced paths and sand/shingle. Access conditions vary and some areas are restricted.

source.reference: Sandwich Bay Sea Fishing Mark, published 18 June 2021
source.location_reference: British Beaches, Sandwich Bay, approximate beach midpoint

marks.parking: Sandwich Bay Estate operates paid vehicle access and an unpaved parking area near the beachfront. Charges and access restrictions apply.

marks.name: Blue Anchor
marks.description: SeaAngler published Blue Anchor as a group of shore marks covering the wall beside the road, the beach in front of the chalets and rocky reefs.
tips: SeaAngler reports the wall and beach fish best on tides over five metres, with larger tides more productive.
SeaAngler warns that the tide retreats a long distance at low water and that mud and quicksand are present.
marks.access: The seafront promenade is long and flat, but Blue Anchor beach access includes steep steps that are not suitable for wheelchairs. The published fishing mark also includes rocky reefs, so accessibility to the fishing positions varies.

source.reference: Blue Anchor Sea Fishing Marks, published 16 June 2021
source.location_reference: British Beaches, Blue Anchor Beach, approximate beach midpoint

marks.parking: Somerset Council lists Blue Anchor Car Park as free, long-stay, 24-hour parking with four disabled bays.

marks.name: White Mark & Gasworks
marks.description: SeaAngler published White Mark and Gasworks as fishing marks to the left of Minehead harbour. White Mark is described as a low-water mark, while Gasworks fishes around dead low water.
tips: SeaAngler reports White Mark fishes around two hours either side of low water.
SeaAngler reports the sand is uncovered at dead low water at Gasworks.
marks.access: SeaAngler directs anglers to the harbour and promenade, then a footpath through the woods to the beach. The White Mark is to the left and Gasworks is in front of the footpath towards the bay.

source.reference: White Mark & Gasworks sea fishing marks, published 16 June 2021
source.location_reference: Minehead harbour/promenade access area; coordinates used are for the verified access/parking area, not an exact fishing position

marks.parking: SeaAngler reports pay-and-display parking along the harbour and promenade.

marks.name: Bossington
marks.description: SeaAngler published Bossington as a steep shingle beach fishing mark on the eastern edge of Porlock Bay.
tips: SeaAngler reports daylight bottom fishing can produce after a strong west wind when the water is coloured.
SeaAngler reports night fishing is more productive in clear conditions.
Morning and evening high tides are reported as good times for float fishing and spinning.
marks.access: SeaAngler says the beach is about a 10-minute walk from the Bossington car park along a rough track. It says driving the track is possible but the track is narrow and badly potholed.

source.reference: Bossington Sea Fishing Mark, published 16 June 2021
source.location_reference: Bossington village/access area; coordinates are for the verified village area, not the exact fishing position

marks.parking: National Trust Bossington car park. National Trust lists accessible parking spaces.
marks.parking_cost: £2 for two hours; £5 all day; free for National Trust members and Blue Badge holders

marks.name: Cheyne Section
marks.description: SeaAngler published Cheyne Section as a rugged flood-tide mark on Portland's eastern flank, with high ledges and a scramble to the water near the old pipe access.
tips: SeaAngler describes Cheyne Section as a flood-tide venue.
SeaAngler says the better ledges are a few hundred yards south of the initial access point.
SeaAngler gives summer and autumn as the season.
marks.access: SeaAngler describes access via a footpath through an old quarry and notes lofty ledges around 40 feet above the sea. A scramble to the water is possible near the old pipe access.

source.reference: Cheyne Section Sea Fishing Mark, published 16 June 2021
source.location_reference: Cheyne Weares parking/access area; coordinates are for the verified access area, not an exact fishing ledge
source.access_reference: Cheyne Weares car park location independently checked

marks.parking: SeaAngler reports some free parking on the left before the yellow lines near Southwell. A separately checked Cheyne Weares car park is also in the access area.
marks.parking_cost: free roadside parking reported by SeaAngler; other nearby parking may have separate charges
